prompt:
Larder now serves two kitchens. Add sites as schema 3:
- Every location belongs to a site (`site` on each location) and the data has a `sites` list. Existing locations belong to site `main`. Add a second site `annex` ("Annex kitchen") with one location `annex-fridge` ("Annex fridge", 4 °C) to data/seed.json.
- A request names its site in the `X-Larder-Site` header; without it the site is `main`. An unknown site is a 400 error with its own error code.
- Batches, stock on hand, cooking, alerts, the stock value report and stock-takes only see the request's site. Items, suppliers, recipes and dishes are shared.
Older data files must still open. Update the tests that assume the old schema.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Sites are added as schema 3. A request picks its site with the `X-Larder-Site` header (default `main`), and an unknown site gets a 400 with the new code `unknown_site`. Batches, stock on hand, cooking, alerts, the stock value report and stock-takes only see that site. Items, suppliers, recipes and dishes are shared. A new migration from schema 2 to 3 puts every existing location in site `main`, so schema 1 and 2 files still open: `larder migrate` upgraded data/db.json 2 → 3 in a temp copy. data/seed.json now has sites `main` and `annex`, with `annex-fridge` (Annex fridge, 4 °C). `npm test` (34 pass, 0 fail) and `npm run lint` both pass. I updated the CLI migrate test and added tests for the migration and for sites. Decisions you should check: (1) Things you didn't list also follow the request's site, because they read site stock: the waste report, forecasts, CSV exports, and receiving an order, which only accepts the site's own locations. Purchase orders and temperature logs stay shared. (2) The nightly job now checks every site, not just the header's, so the annex gets alerts too. Its low-stock key changed from `low:<day>` to `low:<site>:<day>`, so it may queue a second low-stock notice for main on the day you upgrade. (3) Domain functions and the CLI use site `main` when no site is given. (4) data/db.json is left at schema 2; it upgrades when it loads and has no annex site. Problems I found but did not fix, since they are outside the task: temperature limits are looked up by location id (`fridge`, `freezer`), so `annex-fridge` has no 5 °C limit — warm readings show as ok and missed daily checks are not reported. Batches are used newest-received-first instead of first-expired-first, against the rule in docs/DATA.md. The stock value report adds up unrounded amounts before rounding, against the money rule.

check.why: sites through storage, stock, cooking, alerts, reports, stock-takes and docs
